sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Benn Étair is an Irish mythological hill. It is now the Hill of Howth near Dublin. The site appears in many legends. In the tale of the Sons of Tuireann, the weary heroes said their strength would return once they saw Benn Étair. The hill may have held healing power. Aidin, the widow of the hero Oscar, was buried there by the bard Oisin. A fairy woman, Etain of the Fair Hair, lived on the hill. She died of grief when her mortal husband was killed. The hill is named for her father, Étair.

okr.objective: Benn Étair is the Dublin hill whose healing power, burials, and name bind the heroes, bard, and fairy woman of legend.
